faq.q: How much does a house cost in Burnaby?
faq.a: The median Burnaby house sold for $1,850,000 in the year to October 22, 2026, with the middle half between $1,609,500 and $2,220,000. That is $654 a square foot.

faq.q: Which Burnaby neighbourhood has the most house sales?
faq.a: Capitol Hill, with 31 sales and a median of $2,040,000. South Slope was next with 37.

faq.q: How many units can a Burnaby house lot take?
faq.a: Three on a lot of 280 square metres or less, four on a larger lot, and five or six only in a Frequent Transit Neighbourhood Area. Suites count toward the total.
No. It is a Burnaby neighbourhood. Boundary Road is the line with Vancouver, and property taxes are Burnaby’s.

faq.q: How fast do Burnaby houses sell?
faq.a: 28 days at a median, and houses closed at 95.4% of list. 6% went over the list price.

faq.q: Do I need a geotechnical report to build on a Burnaby slope?
faq.a: Burnaby’s application checklist, effective August 1, 2026, asks for a geotechnical report, and for steep-slope sites slope stability and hydrogeological reports as well.

blocks.text: This search lists detached houses for sale in Burnaby, from the north slope above Hastings Street to the lots around Deer Lake and the east side. It leaves out condos, townhomes and half duplexes, which have their own searches.

424 Burnaby houses closed in the year to October 22, 2026 at a median of $1,850,000. 235 of them, 55%, sold for $1,800,000 or more. That puts Burnaby well above Surrey, where the City median was $1,385,000.

blocks.text: Capitol Hill, the hill north of Hastings Street, and Vancouver Heights have median lots of about 4,026 sq ft and 4,049 sq ft. Vancouver Heights is a Burnaby neighbourhood, not part of Vancouver, with Boundary Road as the city line. South Slope, between Rumble Street and Marine Drive, is covered by the Royal Oak Community Plan adopted in March 2025, and its median house sold for $1,860,000.

blocks.text: Since July 1, 2024 nearly every Burnaby house lot sits in the R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District. A lot of 280 square metres (3,014 square feet) or less can take 3 units, a larger lot 4, and 5 to 6 units are possible only in a Frequent Transit Neighbourhood Area. Laneway homes, duplexes, multiplexes and cottage courts are all on the list.

A secondary suite counts toward the lot’s unit total, you get one suite per primary unit, and the suite stays on the same title as the house. Burnaby also has a new Zoning Bylaw 2026, adopted June 9, 2026 and effective July 1, 2026, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025. Trees are protected by Tree Bylaw 10482, so check before you plan to clear a lot.

Slope and water decide a lot of Burnaby building. The City’s application checklist, effective August 1, 2026, asks for a geotechnical report and, on steep sites, slope stability and hydrogeological reports. Lots beside a creek fall under the Streamside Protection and Enhancement Development Permit Area.
Costs of owning a Burnaby house

Burnaby’s 2026 municipal residential rate is $1.72223 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a Metro Vancouver rate of $0.05440. A detached house pays $652.33 for 2026 water and $159 for the default garbage toter. Renting a suite adds $326.17 for water and $403.00 for sewer. Burnaby is a Speculation and Vacancy Tax area.
